text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Lithuanian police are clamping down on the flourishing prostitution business.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas, on an official visit to Japan, urged Japanese companies to participate in the privatisation of key assets in Lithuania's energy, transport and communication sectors.
- A visa-free regime between Lithuania and Finland will come into force three months after the parliaments of the two countries ratify a pact on the readmission of illegal immigrants.
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development intends to particpate in Lithuania's privatisation process.
- The economy ministry is drafting a project to impose a 17 percent tax on fuel products imported from countries which Lithuania has not signed free-trade pacts with.
- The Lithuanian government has proposed to raise the rates on banking deposit insurance.
- Siauliu Bank reported a 208,000 litas net profit in April and 568,000 litas for the first four months of the year.

- The year-on-year inflation rate in April in Lithuania was 7.3 percent, the lowest among the Baltic countries. In Latvia the annual inflation rate reached 8.8 percent in April while it was 9.2 percent in Estonia.
